summary.en: Repeated occasions often have their own ending pattern.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 2, 4 and 6.

To say *every Tuesday*, *every Friday* or *every morning*, Russian uses a form of **каждый** (*every / each*) directly with the time noun—no extra preposition needed: **каждый вторник** (*every Tuesday*), **каждую пятницу** (*every Friday*), and **каждое утро** (*every morning*).

Because **каждый** behaves like an adjective, its ending changes to match the gender and case of the noun that follows. In direct time expressions (accusative case), masculine **вторник** takes **каждый**, feminine **пятница** shifts to **каждую пятницу**, and neuter **утро** takes **каждое утро**.

Outside time expressions, **каждый** also means *each* with everyday objects, taking whatever case the preposition requires—for instance, Zoya asks Matvey to set a spoon **у каждой синей чашки** (*by each blue cup*).

On replay, listen to **каждый**, **каждую** or **каждое** together with its noun as one rhythmic unit telling you either how often something happens or which individual items are meant.
